transcript:
00:00 Olivia Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, uh, Olivia from Redwood here. Marcus is with me, SE.
00:08 Sanjay Rao: Hey Olivia, Leah, Tom on the line. Good to be back.
00:14 Olivia Chen: Awesome. Quick agenda — run through the latest POC run results, focus on SDK tool/function call patterns and the problem with structured output getting malformed occasionally, then tuning recommendations and next steps.
00:28 Marcus Lee: I can start with the results summary if that's cool. We re-ran your sample integration three times last week with the same prompt set — about 300 requests total.
00:36 Tom Alvarez: Right, we saw the sheet you uploaded. There were a couple of big latency outliers and some malformed JSON payloads.
00:45 Marcus Lee: Exactly. Baseline median p95 was about 420ms outbound from your app to Redwood hosted endpoint when we pinned the dedicated variant. The outliers up near 2.1s correlated with cold-batch windows and when prefix caching wasn't hit.
01:00 Leah Kim: On the malformed JSON — that's the one that breaks our parser. Sometimes the SDK returns an incomplete object or escapes are wrong. Could be transcription, or tokenization cutting off?
01:12 Marcus Lee: Yeah, likely a few things. We saw two classes of failures: (1) truncated output because the streaming connection was interrupted mid-response — we saw TCP resets in a couple logs — and (2) model-generated outputs that don't match the expected schema. For the latter, we recommended stricter schema enforcement via post-parse validation and fallback logic.
01:30 Olivia Chen: To be clear, VectorPay is using our SDK call pattern in the typical tool-calling mode, right? Where you declare functions and the model picks a function name?
01:38 Leah Kim: Correct. We're using the function calling wrapper — declared about five tool functions. Our app expects a JSON object with fields: action, payload, confidence.
01:48 Marcus Lee: Two practical suggestions: add a deterministic wrapper around function outputs — e.g., require model to return a single top-level JSON string and run a small sanitizer that strips trailing tokens before JSON.parse; and enable Redwood's structured-output option that enforces a JSON schema server-side.
02:02 Tom Alvarez: Is the structured-output enforcement available on hosted or only on Dedicated? Because we're evaluating Dedicated but initial plan was hosted.
02:09 Olivia Chen: Good question. Structured-output schema checks are available on both; on Dedicated you can push custom schema into the config and set stricter rejection policies, but hosted also supports schema validation at the API layer with configurable tolerance.
02:22 Sanjay Rao: What's the impact on latency if we enforce strict server-side schema validation?
02:27 Marcus Lee: In our tests the additional validation step added about 10-25ms median, so minimal. The bigger latency wins/losses come from batching and KV cache hit rates. If you increase batch sizes aggressively you can drop unit cost but p95 will rise.
02:45 Leah Kim: On the SDK side, we're using the JS client with streaming. We're concerned that streaming + function calls + structured output is the edge case causing the truncation. Is there a recommended pattern?
02:55 Marcus Lee: For streaming + function calls we recommend: stream to client but buffer until function response is complete on server side; then emit a final verified JSON chunk. Also enable auto-retry for transient 5xx with exponential backoff and idempotency key so duplicates don't cause side effects.
03:18 Tom Alvarez: We also saw one case where the 'confidence' numeric came as a string, and that broke the reducer in our product pipeline. Is that on our side or model?
03:28 Marcus Lee: Model sometimes emits numbers as strings depending on prompt framing. We suggest adding a strict schema with types and a small normalization step post-parse. We'll include a snippet in the sample SDK repo.
03:40 Olivia Chen: On the experimental side, Leah — we ran a quantized variant in the Dedicated pool to save cost. Quality held up for this workload, but we saw slightly higher variance in tokenization on boundary tokens. Not huge, but something to keep an eye on.
03:55 Sanjay Rao: So action items: code examples, logs, and the 1k-run. Anything else?
04:03 Marcus Lee: Also, I will export the latency breakdown showing the time spent in model execution vs network vs request queuing so you can map to your infra.
04:12 Leah Kim: That will help. Also on security — Tom will coordinate a session with infra to talk VPC peering, SAML, and audit logs. Is Redwood able to share SOC2 docs ahead of that?
04:24 Olivia Chen: Yes, we'll share the SOC2 and the standard security pack. For Dedicated, we can add KMS integration notes. I'll drop the link in the follow-up email.
04:36 Tom Alvarez: One more question — we tested a fallback policy to a smaller model when Dedicated capacity was pegged. There was some regression in structured output shape. Any recommendations?
04:48 Marcus Lee: When fallback to model variants, keep a strict schema validation and a lightweight post-processor that maps variant outputs into canonical fields. Also consider model-aware prompts that include explicit type hints. We'll share a prompt template that reduces schema drift.
05:05 Leah Kim: For the malformed JSON examples, can you attach the raw streaming logs so we can reproduce?
05:11 Marcus Lee: Yep, we'll attach the server logs and the client-side traces we captured. Expect those in the shared sheet.
05:19 Olivia Chen: Great. Quick recap of next steps: Olivia to send SDK snippet/sample repo, Marcus to share latency breakdown and logs, Leah to run the 1k e2e test, Tom to schedule security deep dive. We'll target follow-up the first week of January.
05:35 Sanjay Rao: Sounds good. Any risks we should call out?
05:39 Marcus Lee: Main risk is parser breakage in production if malformed outputs slip through; mitigation is schema validation + retries + idempotency. Another is underestimated p95 under heavy load — we'll bench that.
05:52 Olivia Chen: Okay, thanks all. We'll email the artifacts right after. Have a good one.
05:58 Tom Alvarez: Thanks everyone. Bye.
06:00 [meeting end]
